title: fix(analytics): a dataset filter key that names an object field filters that field, whatever a dimension is named
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XJmYB6Mne14zoqpZuAboc2M)_

Fixes #25814

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## What was wrong

A dashboard global filter's `field` resolves against the dataset's object, not its dimensions (`GlobalFilterSchema.field`). The authoring gates read a widget `filter`, a dataset `filter` and a measure `filter` the same way (`widget-filter-field-unknown`, `dataset-filter-field-unknown`), and so does the draft-preview face, which matches `row[key]`.

`DatasetExecutor` hands those filters to `AnalyticsService.query()` as the compiled cube's `where`. Both strategies, and the field-read admission in front of them, resolve a `where` key through the cube's MEMBERS first (`lookupMember` / `declaredMemberEntry`). So with a dimension `{ name: 'department', field: 'department.name' }`, `runtimeFilter: { department: 'bu_1' }` became the following on `main` (05f7758f05):

- NativeSQLStrategy: `... LEFT JOIN "department" ... WHERE "department"."name" = $1`, bound to `bu_1`, so 0 rows.
- ObjectQLStrategy: refused as `cannot evaluate a cross-object filter ("department.name")`.

## The fix

`dataset-filter-field-binding.ts` (new), called once in `answerDataset` on the published path. A filter key is SHADOWED when two things hold: it names a field of the dataset object (`getObjectFieldNames`, plus `id` / `created_at` / `updated_at`, the same set `assertWhereFields` uses), and a cube member resolves it to a different `sql`. Each shadowed key is bound, for that request only, to a member minted on the request scope's copy of the cube whose `sql` IS the field. The selection's `runtimeFilter`, the dataset `filter` and every measure `filter` are rewritten onto that member.

Every downstream reader then resolves the field the author wrote with the rule it already uses: the native compiler, the ObjectQL hand-off, the SQL echo and the field-read admission. What the gate judges and what reaches SQL therefore cannot diverge, and no second resolution rule was added to any strategy. The minted member exists only in the `queryDataset` request scope (#20356), which `getMeta` never publishes and which is dropped with the call.

The following are unchanged, each pinned:

- A key that is not an object field keeps today's answer (`department_name: 'Legal'` still goes through the dimension).
- The cube door: `/analytics/query` on a registered dataset's cube still reads `where` as member names.
- A host whose `getObjectFieldNames` cannot answer keeps today's resolution. This is the "cannot answer, do not block" tier of the sibling field gates. `AnalyticsServicePlugin` wires the probe.
- The draft-preview face already matched by field and is not touched.
- A key carrying a nested-relation condition is left as written; see Acceptance notes.

`isNestedRelationCondition` in `strategies/filter-normalizer.ts` is now exported within the package, so the binding reads the same predicate the normalizer does instead of carrying a copy. It is not re-exported from the package index, so the public surface is unchanged.

Scope note: the claim's surface is `runtimeFilter`. The dataset `filter` and measure `filter` travel in the same `where` / dataset-scope channel and are object-field keys under the same lint rules. Binding only `runtimeFilter` would make one query resolve one key two ways (a runtime filter and a dataset filter on `department` would AND a base column with a joined one). They are bound by the same helper, in the same file, and pinned by the same test file.

## Where a `runtimeFilter` key is resolved (the order's measurement)

| Door | Path | Rule after this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Dashboard / report widget (`POST /analytics/dataset/query`, build probes) | `queryDataset` → `answerDataset` → `DatasetExecutor.executeSelection` → `query()` | object field (bound) |
| Draft preview (`previewDrafts`) | `evaluateAnalyticsQueryOverRows` → `matchesWhere(row[key])` | object field (already) |
| Cube door `/analytics/query`, `/analytics/sql` | `query()` / `generateSql()`, no `runtimeFilter`, `where` is member vocabulary | unchanged (member first) |
| Export | none: no server-side `runtimeFilter` reader outside the dataset door in `packages/**` (measured: `git grep runtimeFilter` at 05f7758f05 finds only the analytics service, its REST door and lint) | n/a |

## Clause-② measurement

`Clause-②: no`. No input is refused that was accepted, no surface is widened. The change is the answer for a shadowed key. Measured at `origin/main` 05f7758f05: the five in-repo datasets (`examples/app-crm/src/datasets/opportunity.dataset.ts`, `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/datasets/chart-gallery.dataset.ts`, `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/datasets/revenue-pulse.dataset.ts`, `examples/app-todo/src/datasets/task.dataset.ts`, `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/dashboards/system.datasets.ts`) declare 26 dimensions. Every one has `field` equal to its `name`, so no dimension shadows a field and no in-repo app or example relies on dimension-first through a dimension. Measure names, which shadow only when they equal an object field, were not measured against each object's field list. The only producer known to meet the collision is hotclm, which renamed its dimension.

## Tests (head 7b7ccb85; the code commit is ea1d9a38, and 7b7ccb85 only edits the changeset text)

- Red first: the new `dataset-filter-object-field-binding.test.ts` against the unfixed service gives 6 failed, 4 passed. The 4 that pass are the controls: the dimension-only key, the probe that cannot answer, the cube door, and the refusal of an unreadable field. Example: `expected '"department"."name" = $1' to be '"clm_contract"."department" = $1'`. The base-column spelling was later corrected to the bare form the compiler emits for a join-less statement.
- Green: 13/13 in that file.
- Ablation (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor x1 → x0, blob 319c5b97 → 3dd0092d): replacing the binding call with the identity gives 6 failed, 7 passed. Restored blob 319c5b97 equals the HEAD blob, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-analytics typecheck && vitest run --maxWorkers=2` (under the verify lock, at ea1d9a38): 189 test files passed, 4576 tests passed, 282 skipped, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `eslint --no-inline-config packages/services/service-analytics`: exit 0, no findings.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives 70 families. 68 ran with exit 0. Two answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3) and are NOT MEASURED locally: `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` (shallow clone cannot read its pinned fixture) and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (needs a full `pnpm build`). Both run in CI's Lint & Repo Gates. `--ran` reconciliation: 70 derived, 68 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. After the changeset-text commit, the changeset, ADR-0087, empty-changeset, nul-bytes, issue-citations and doc-authoring gates were re-run on 7b7ccb85, all exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

- A key carrying a nested-relation condition (`{ department: { name: 'Legal' } }`) is not bound. ObjectQLStrategy emits that form to the engine as written, keyed by the raw field, but its cross-object planner (`filterMemberView`) resolves the same key through the cube. With a shadowing dimension, the planner therefore refuses it as a cross-object filter on `department.name`. That is today's answer and it is loud. Binding the key would fix the planner but leak the minted name into the engine filter, so the right fix is in the strategy. Reported to the seat as a finding, not fixed here.
- A dotted key whose TAIL equals a dimension name (`{ 'account.region': … }` beside a dimension `region`) resolves through `lookupMember`'s legacy "plain second-segment" tier to that dimension. This is a different shadowing tier and is not measured end to end here. Noted only.
- The minted member can appear in the "Valid filter members" list of an `INVALID_FIELD` refusal from `assertWhereFields`, and only when a shadowed key and an invalid key arrive in the same request. It resolves to the real field, so the suggestion is not wrong.
